summary: This program collects party RSVP names in a TreeSet, which automatically discards duplicate names and keeps the remaining ones sorted. It then prints how many unique guests replied, followed by the guest list in alphabetical order.

lines.text: TreeSet is the sorted implementation of Set, so it must be imported before it can be used.
The Set interface is imported separately because the variable below is declared with the interface type rather than the concrete class.
Declaring the variable as a Set while creating a TreeSet means the code only relies on general set behaviour, so the implementation could be swapped later without rewriting the rest of the method.
Each add call offers one name to the set; a TreeSet stores it in sorted position instead of at the end.
Adding a name that is already present changes nothing, because a set holds at most one copy of each value.
The size is 6 rather than 8, which shows that the two duplicate entries were silently rejected.
Looping over a TreeSet visits the elements in their natural order, so String values come out alphabetically without any sorting code.
Prefixing each name with a dash formats the output as a readable bulleted guest list.
